title: Elevated error rate after deploy traced to a missing feature-flag default
notes: Incident response: bad deploy causes elevated error rates, rollback decision, root-cause lesson, follow-up todo.

turns.text: Error rate on checkout jumped from ~0.2% to ~9% right after the 2:15pm deploy. Can you take a look?

Looking at the error logs now — most of the errors are 'undefined is not a function' on getShippingEstimate(), which is behind the new express-shipping feature flag. The flag lookup is throwing instead of returning false when the flag key doesn't exist in the flag store yet.
Roll it back while we figure out the fix.
Rolled back to the previous deploy. Error rate dropped back to ~0.2% within about 90 seconds of rollback completing.
So what actually went wrong with the flag?

The new code assumed the express-shipping flag key would already exist in the flag store (defaulting to false), but the flag was never actually created there before this deploy shipped — the flag-store entry and the code that reads it were supposed to ship together but the flag creation step got missed.
Fix that properly before we redeploy.

I'll make the flag lookup default to false when the key is missing, instead of throwing, as defense in depth — and separately, create the express-shipping flag entry in the flag store now so the intended behavior is available once we redeploy.
Good. Let's also make sure this class of bug can't repeat.
Adding a todo: audit the deploy checklist to require confirming any new feature-flag key exists in the flag store before the code referencing it ships, not after.

gold_atoms.text: Checkout error rate jumped from about 0.2% to about 9% shortly after the 2:15pm deploy, caused by getShippingEstimate() throwing on lookup of the new express-shipping feature flag.
Rolled back the deploy to stop the elevated checkout error rate; error rate returned to about 0.2% within roughly 90 seconds of rollback completing.

The new deploy assumed the express-shipping feature flag key already existed in the flag store, but the flag-store entry was never created before the deploy shipped, and the flag lookup threw instead of defaulting to false for a missing key.
Make the feature-flag lookup default to false when a flag key is missing, instead of throwing, as defense in depth; also create the missing express-shipping flag entry before redeploying.
Audit the deploy checklist to require confirming any new feature-flag key exists in the flag store before the code referencing it ships.
